newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - July 21.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - July 21.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Philippine stocks on Monday:
* Traders expect the market to sustain its upbeat mood as lowering of overnight rates signalled some stability in the foreign exchange market.

* Buying momentum will continue early this week and the 2,750 point resistance may be tested, said Sun Hung Kai Securities. The direction of the market will largely be determined by how the Central Bank manages interest rates and the peso.

* Asian Capital Equities chief technical analyst Jonathan Ravelas said his firm continues to maintain a positive outlook on the market. He said technical analysis show the composite index is still within its ascending trendline since October 1990.
* On Friday, the Philippine composite index closed sharply higher for the second day, rising 52.57 points at 2,672.95 points.
* The Dow Jones on Friday ended 130.11 points lower at 7,890.46. PLDT's ADR closed up $0/11 at $33/07
* The Philippine peso ended unchanged at 28 pesos to a dollar.
* The Philippine interbank call loan average at 25.09375 percent vs 28.1875 percent.
* Philippine President Fidel Ramos said on Sunday the stability of the peso after its recent weakness proved wrong "doomsayers" who had predicted the country's economic collapse.
* Central Bank governor Gabriel Singson said it hoped to make further cuts in the overnight borrowing rate if the currenct market continued to stabilise.

* The International Monetary Fund (IMF) offered the Philippines almost $1.1 billion in financial support on Friday to help ease the problems caused by a currency crash. The loan, $699 million of it to be available immediately, extended $652 million from an existing three-year Extended Fund Facility (EFF) credit line until the end of this year and added $435 million of extra cash, the IMF said.
* MacroAsia Corp said on Friday it was negotiating with Philippine Airlines to take over its ground services.

* The Philippine government and the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) signed an agreement to enforce a ceasefire and resume their peace negotiations. The MILF is a separatist Moslem group battling for an Islamic state in the southern Mindanao island.
* Newspaper BusinessWorld said the Central Bank expects the peso to continue its recovery this week on the back of increased dollar supply and renewed foreign investor interest in the Philippines.

* The Board of Investments (BOI) has relaxed its debt-to-equity ratio requirement imposed on projects seeking government tax and fiscal incentives. Trade Undersecretary Melito Salazar said the BOI would not require a strict 75:25 debt-to-equity ratio in their project financing but a reasonable ratio. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
* Manila Standard said Petron Corp may or may not increase prices of petroleum products this month, depending on the movement of the peso-dollar exchange rate this week.
